runs.a1_t07_3: model. Plain loop, sampled. Fixed the tie bug, then ran the tests again and again and concluded the apostrophe test itself was wrong ("the test may have an error in its expectations"). Same loop, same model passed the other three runs.
runs.a3_1: framework contract. Pydantic AI, greedy. Both bugs fixed and tests passing by call 8; the model then answered in a sentence, which Pydantic AI rejects because the result must come through its final_result tool. The validation error went back as a retry prompt, the model started re-editing a file that was already fixed, and the run hit the 15-request limit (UsageLimitExceeded). Repository fixed.
runs.a3_t07_1: framework contract. Both bugs fixed, then a plain-text summary instead of a final_result call, twice: UnexpectedModelBehavior: Exceeded maximum output retries (1). Repository fixed.
runs.a3_t07_2: model, then the limit. Fixed the apostrophe bug, never fixed the tie bug although it kept re-examining that test, hit the 15-request limit.
runs.a3_t07_3: framework contract. Same as a3_t07_1: repository fixed, output retries exhausted.
runs.a4_1: model. OpenAI Agents SDK, greedy. Fixed the tie bug, never ran the tests, and stopped with "The tests should now pass." The SDK did what it was told: a reply without a tool call ends the run, exactly as in the plain loop. The three sampled runs passed.
runs.a5_1: code actions plus model. smolagents, greedy. The model's code did for f in list_files() over our newline-separated string and read the file names as single letters, decided the module was missing, tried to write a new textstats.py (blocked: open is not allowed in the local executor) and ended with a final_answer claiming success.
runs.a5_t07_1: format plus model. Fixed only the tie bug; no test output ever reached its observations, so it never saw the failing apostrophe test; lost steps to code-block format errors and used all 15 steps.
runs.a5_t07_2: model. Fixed only the tie bug, ended with final_answer("The tests now pass ...").
runs.a5_t07_3: model. Fixed only the tie bug and called final_answer after five calls without running the tests.
runs.a5b_1: framework history format. smolagents ToolCallingAgent. The model's first two tool calls were native; smolagents then wrote them back into the history as plain text (Calling tools: [{'id': ..., 'function': ...}], Python repr with single quotes) and the results as user messages starting "Observation:". The model imitated that text, which smolagents' JSON parser rejects (about 8 error observations); out of steps with one bug fixed.
runs.a5b_t07_1: framework history format, as a5b_1; one edit also left a regex with a syntax error.
runs.a5b_t07_2: framework history format, as a5b_1 (about 9 error observations).

summary: Reading it fairly. With the same 4B model, the plain loop fixed 3 of 4 runs and LangGraph 4 of 4: the model can do this task when the conversation is the plain native format. Pydantic AI fixed the code in 3 of 4 runs but ended none cleanly: its typed-result contract (a mandatory final_result tool) is what this model did not follow. The OpenAI Agents SDK lost one run to the model stopping early, as a plain loop can. smolagents fixed none of 8 runs, with code actions and without them; the ToolCallingAgent transcripts show why: smolagents sends past tool calls back as text in its own format ("Calling tools:\n" + str([...]) in 1.26.0's memory.py) rather than as native tool-call messages, and a small model copies the text. Every Claude run passed; that is a stronger model, not a better framework. The 4B model's failures say how much slack each framework's prompt and format leave a weak model, which is worth knowing if you plan to run small local models.
